title: Round 10 / ECDLP-34: rational (with division) x-only interpolation bound and SLP barrier in Lean
question: SLP barrier with division (x-only): over a field F (2 != 0), W short Weierstrass, P of order r, 2N < r. Any straight-line program over F with +, −, ×, ÷ and constants, single input u = x(Q), in which every division is defined (nonzero divisor) at every u = x(kP), 1 <= k <= N, and whose output equals k at u = x(kP), has length L >= log2((N − c)/c') for explicit constants (expected: the output is a rational function g = A/B of degree max(deg A, deg B) <= 2^L, and a rational analogue of Theorem C gives N <= 3·deg + O(1) or similar).
claims: Formal (Lean, axioms propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound only): for division SLPs over a field F (2 != 0) on a short Weierstrass curve, P of order r, 2N<r, if every division is defined at each x(kP) and output = k there for 1<=k<=N then N <= 3*2^L + 2 (MathResearch.ECDLP.RationalSLP.length_bound_rational_slp).

Formal rational analogue of Theorem C: A,B in F[X] of degree <= d, B(x_k)!=0, A(x_k)=k B(x_k) for 1<=k<=N, 2N<r imply N <= 3d+2; nonvanishing of the cleared polynomial proved by orbit propagation (no extra hypothesis). Empirical toy-curve checks only for identities and minimal degrees (~N/2). Not a bit-complexity or hardness claim.
